best_for: Hobby animators and small studios who want to tween vector characters and cutout puppets without paying for an animation suite.

points.title: Tweening does the in-betweens
points.text: You set key poses and Synfig works out the frames between them. That cuts down hand drawing, so one person can finish longer scenes.

points.title: Bones for cutout rigs
points.text: A bone system moves vector art or bitmap images as cutout puppets, and a Skeleton Distortion layer bends artwork along the bones. Parameters can also be linked to each other or driven by math expressions.

points.title: Over 50 layer types
points.text: Layers cover shapes, gradients, filters, distortions, transforms and fractals. Effects live in the layer stack rather than in separate plugins.

points.title: Free, with an optional $2
points.text: Synfig is GPL-3.0 open source. The download page offers a free download next to a $2 purchase button, and says you do not have to pay.

points.title: The Mac build trails behind
points.text: Windows and Linux are listed here at 1.5.3, while macOS is at 1.4.5. Homebrew disabled its cask on 2026-09-01 because the app fails Apple's Gatekeeper check, so expect a security prompt when you first open it on a Mac.

points.title: Linux Flatpak comes from Synfig
points.text: The Flathub build is verified as published by Synfig, for x64 and Arm64. Windows gets 32-bit and 64-bit installers that install for all users.

points.title: One version per platform
points.text: This site keeps only the current release for Windows, macOS and Linux, so older versions need another source, such as the project's GitHub releases.
